The Standard 4.0 College GPA Scale

Grade Point Average (GPA) is the universal metric used by higher education institutions to measure academic performance. Letter grades correspond to standard numerical grade points:

  • A / A+: 4.0 Grade Points
  • A-: 3.7 Grade Points
  • B+: 3.3 Grade Points
  • B: 3.0 Grade Points
  • B-: 2.7 Grade Points
  • C+: 2.3 Grade Points
  • C: 2.0 Grade Points
  • D: 1.0 Grade Point
  • F: 0.0 Grade Points

The Mathematical Formula for Cumulative GPA

To calculate your semester or cumulative GPA manually:

Cumulative GPA = (Total Grade Points Earned) / (Total Credit Hours Attempted)

Step-by-Step Calculation Example

  1. Multiply each course's grade points by its credit hours to find quality points.
  2. Sum up all quality points across all completed semesters.
  3. Divide total quality points by total credit hours.

blogPosts.content:
Introduction to Web Hosting

Building a website begins with a solid foundation: web hosting. Whether you are launching a personal portfolio, an e-commerce store, or a business blog, your choice of hosting provider directly influences your site's speed, security, uptime, and search engine rankings.

With hundreds of web hosting companies operating globally, choosing the right provider can feel overwhelming. This guide explores the core fundamentals of web hosting, key features to evaluate, and what to consider before purchasing a plan.

What is Web Hosting and Why Does It Matter?

Think of web hosting as renting digital real estate on the internet. Your website files—HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, and databases—must live on a powerful computer (a server) that remains connected to the internet 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. When a user types your domain name into their browser, their computer requests those files from your hosting server.

If your host is slow or unreliable, visitors will experience lagging page loads or error screens (such as 504 Gateway Timeouts), leading to high bounce rates and lost revenue.

Core Types of Web Hosting

Different websites have vastly different traffic and resource demands. Understanding hosting tiers helps you select the appropriate architecture:

  • Shared Hosting: Multiple websites share the resources of a single physical server. It is the most cost-effective option, perfect for beginners, blogs, and low-to-medium traffic portfolio sites.
  • Virtual Private Server (VPS) Hosting: A physical server is partitioned into multiple virtual servers, giving each user dedicated RAM and CPU allocations. Ideal for growing businesses and high-traffic applications.
  • Cloud Hosting: Your website is hosted across a cluster of interconnected cloud servers. If one server experiences hardware issues, another seamlessly takes over, ensuring near-100% uptime.
  • WordPress Hosting: Specialized hosting optimized specifically for WordPress CMS performance, featuring pre-installed caching, automated core updates, and specialized security firewalls.

Critical Factors to Evaluate Before Choosing a Host

Before committing to a web hosting provider, evaluate these essential performance metrics:

  1. Uptime Guarantee: Look for providers offering at least 99.9% uptime. Downtime means potential customers cannot reach your business.
  2. Page Load Speed & NVMe Storage: Modern hosts utilizing NVMe SSD drives deliver significantly faster file read/write speeds than legacy mechanical hard drives.
  3. Free SSL Certificates: Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) encrypts data transmitted between your visitor and your server, vital for user trust and Google rankings.

A robots.txt file is a standard text file located at the root of your web server. It communicates with web crawlers (such as Googlebot and Bingbot), specifying which pages or directories they are allowed or disallowed to crawl.

Essential Robots.txt Directives

  • User-agent: * — Applies rules to all web crawlers.
  • Disallow: /admin/ — Prevents crawlers from scanning administrative dashboards.
  • Allow: /public/ — Explicitly allows access to specific subfolders inside a blocked parent directory.
  • Sitemap: https://yourdomain.com/sitemap.xml — Points crawlers directly to your XML sitemap index.

Step-by-Step: Generating Robots.txt Online

  1. Open the Mehzan Robots.txt Generator Tool.
  2. Select default crawler access rules (Allow or Refuse).
  3. Enter restricted directory paths (e.g., /cart, /admin, /private).
  4. Add your XML sitemap URL and click Generate Robots.txt.
  5. Download the generated robots.txt file and upload it to your server root.

Why XML Sitemaps Are Critical for SEO

An XML sitemap serves as a roadmap for search engines, listing all indexable URLs on your site alongside metadata such as when the page was last updated (lastmod), how frequently it changes (changefreq), and its relative importance (priority).

How to Generate an XML Sitemap

  1. Visit the Mehzan XML Sitemap Generator Tool.
  2. Enter your website URL and specify link discovery preferences.
  3. Click Generate Sitemap.
  4. Download sitemap.xml and upload it to your web server root.
  5. Submit the sitemap link in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.

What Are UTM Parameters?

UTM (Urchin Tracking Module) parameters are five standard query strings appended to a web URL to help analytics tools (like Google Analytics 4) track traffic sources, mediums, and marketing campaign performance.

The 5 Core UTM Parameters

  • utm_source — Identifies the advertiser, site, or publication (e.g. newsletter, linkedin).
  • utm_medium — Identifies the advertising or marketing medium (e.g. email, cpc, social).
  • utm_campaign — Identifies the specific strategic campaign (e.g. summer_sale, product_launch).
  • utm_term — Used primarily for paid search keywords.
  • utm_content — Used to differentiate similar content or links within the same ad or email.

Step-by-Step: Creating Tracking Links

  1. Open the Mehzan UTM Builder Tool.
  2. Paste your target destination website URL.
  3. Enter utm_source, utm_medium, and utm_campaign.
  4. Copy the generated campaign URL or generate a tracking QR code using the Mehzan QR Code Generator.
